forces: Two solo violins and solo cello, ripieno strings and basso continuo
performers: Advent Chamber Orchestra; Roxanna Pavel Goldstein, musical director
intro: Four slow bars, then the violins are off. The Advent Chamber Orchestra plays Corelli’s D-major concerto, its two solo violins chasing one another through the opening Allegro.

sections.label: Intro · Four slow bars
sections.mNote: The strings pause on A major

sections.label: A · The violins chase one another
sections.mNote: One solo violin begins; the second answers

sections.label: A · The first violin starts again

cues.title: Four bars of Adagio
cues.text: The strings open together in D major, pausing after short phrases. Four bars are enough: the last one rests on A major, waiting for the first violin to set the Allegro running.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed p. 56, bars 1–5: four Adagio bars, the A-major dominant and the Allegro entry. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The second violin answers
cues.text: The first solo violin starts alone; the second follows with the same running figure. The larger string group joins their conversation, then steps back. Corelli’s small solo group consists of two violins and a cello.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 56–58, bars 5–25. The 1714 title specifies the concertino of two violins and cello. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf ; https://imslp.org/wiki/12_Concerti_Grossi,_Op.6_(Corelli,_Arcangelo)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Twelve concertos reach Amsterdam
cues.text: In 1714 the Amsterdam publisher Estienne Roger issues Corelli’s twelve concerti grossi as Op. 6. The title page allows the larger string parts to be doubled: more players can join the two solo violins and cello.
cues.evidence: The collection’s 1714 publication details and original title, including “che si potranno radoppiare”, are recorded at https://imslp.org/wiki/12_Concerti_Grossi,_Op.6_(Corelli,_Arcangelo).

cues.title: A phrase changes hands
cues.text: The second section starts in A major. One solo violin runs while the other rests, then they exchange roles. The bass moves steadily beneath the conversation as the harmony works its way back to D.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 59–61, bars 26–51: alternating concertino figures and the return to D major. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Printed after his death
cues.text: Corelli dies on 8 January 1713. His friend Matteo Fornari sees the twelve concerti grossi into print in Amsterdam, with a dedication to Johann Wilhelm, Elector Palatine, dated 20 November 1714. Op. 6 is the only collection of concertos Corelli published.
cues.evidence: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani (Treccani), Corelli entry: he died in the night before 8 January 1713; his will leaves Op. 6 and his papers to Matteo Fornari; Roger’s Amsterdam edition of Op. 6 is undated but carries Fornari’s dedication to the Elector Palatine, signed in Rome on 20 November 1714; Opp. 1–4 are trio sonatas, Op. 5 violin sonatas and Op. 6 the concerti grossi: https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/arcangelo-corelli_(Dizionario-Biografico)/ . Publication details also at IMSLP: https://imslp.org/wiki/12_Concerti_Grossi,_Op.6_(Corelli,_Arcangelo)

cues.title: The second section again
cues.text: A D-major cadence sends the music back to the start of the second section. The solo violins exchange their phrases once more, and the bass brings them home to D again.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 59–61: repeat of bars 26–51. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: A major releases the first violin
transitions.to: A · The violins chase one another
transitions.how: The Adagio holds an A-major chord, the dominant of D. The bass and accompanying strings stop, leaving the first solo violin to begin the Allegro alone. The second solo violin follows with the same quick figure.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed p. 56, bars 4–7. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

transitions.title: Back to the solitary violin
transitions.from: A · The violins chase one another
transitions.to: A · The first violin starts again
transitions.how: The first section closes in A major. Its repeat sends the music straight back to the unaccompanied first violin at the start of the Allegro. The slow introduction stays behind, and the second violin answers again.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 56–58: repeat from bar 25 to bar 5. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

transitions.title: The violins exchange the running line
transitions.from: A · The first violin starts again
transitions.to: B · The violins trade running phrases
transitions.how: After the A-major cadence, the first solo violin sets off again over the bass. This time the second violin waits for its partner’s phrase to finish before taking over the running notes. The two trade places as the bass steps through changing harmonies.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 58–59, bars 25–29. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

transitions.title: D major sends the violins back
transitions.from: B · The violins trade running phrases
transitions.how: The bass reaches D and the strings complete their cadence. The repeat returns to the second section’s A-major opening, with the running line again passed between the solo violins. Its final cadence brings the bass back to D.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 59–61: repeat of bars 26–51. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

timeline.note: The solo group and larger strings play four slow bars together.
The first solo violin starts the Allegro alone; the second violin answers.
The solo violins exchange quick figures, and the larger string group joins them.
The first solo violin begins the Allegro again.
The two solo violins and larger string group repeat their exchanges.
The two solo violins alternate running figures over a moving bass.
The second section repeats and closes in D major.
